candidates.trace: LimbWeights has four public f32 fields and derives Default, which gives four zero weights. Its public normalize sums the four fields and divides each field by that total without a zero or finite guard. Applied symbolically to the default, each numerator and the total are 0.0, so each 0.0/0.0 result is NaN under IEEE floating-point rules. The public attribute and physical-skill functions accept the same structure and use each weight in weighted calculations; for finite attributes and healthy inputs the raw unnormalized all-zero weights contribute zero. Preset both_arms, both_legs and all_equal produce positive unit sums, and the selected normal combat callers use these presets. No method was executed.
candidates.safeguards_and_limits: The existing source does not specify whether a zero weight vector is a meaningful no-limb state, an invalid input to normalization, or intended to be replaced by another policy. No actual production call normalizing Default or consuming its result is demonstrated; selected preset call sites do not establish every consumer or cross-crate caller. Public field construction also permits other sums and nonfinite values, but their admitted policy and effect remain open. This is not a claim of an observed gameplay failure.
candidates.connected_repair: Determine the semantic owner and admission/operation policy for finite weights, sums, and a legitimate zero/no-limb case across producers and attribute/skill consumers. Then make normalization explicitly total or fallible as appropriate, preserving valid individual zero weights and existing named presets rather than inventing a uniform fallback or forbidding zero without a design decision.
candidates.acceptance: After separate implementation authorization, cover intended zero, positive and nonfinite inputs and named preset/weighted calculations according to the chosen policy; trace all callers and serialized boundaries first. Product validation remains deferred.
